subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Perceived quality of the airline SERVICE experience across passenger touchpoints (cabin crew, ground handling, disruption management, customer-service resolution) — including whether that service is perceived to be declining.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attitude
per_column.rationale: Directly characterises in-flight staff service — a core touchpoint of the inferred service-quality focus, with nuanced non-trivial categories.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: This is a product/catering facet rather than a service-interaction touchpoint; it sits on the periphery of a service-quality focus and pulls the set toward general 'experience aspects'.

per_column.name: service_decline_perception
per_column.rationale: Captures whether the reviewer perceives a deterioration in service — squarely on-focus, though it substantially overlaps with airline_decline_narrative.

per_column.name: amenity_and_product_gap
per_column.rationale: Amenity/product provisioning is a product dimension, not a service-interaction quality; contributes to breadth rather than to the service focus.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A distinct service touchpoint (pre-flight ground handling) — a coherent facet of the service-quality focus.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: How disruptions are managed is a high-signal service touchpoint; well-differentiated categories at a useful granularity.

per_column.name: cs_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Post-contact customer-service resolution is another service touchpoint; complements the journey-based decomposition.

per_column.name: airline_decline_narrative
per_column.rationale: On-focus (perceived decline) but near-duplicative of service_decline_perception; both are booleans with almost identical distributions, adding little incremental structure.

per_column.name: premium_cabin_value_judgment
per_column.rationale: A value-for-money/product-tier judgment rather than a service-interaction quality; another dimension that widens the set beyond a single focus.

judge.rationale: A clear majority of columns (cabin crew, ground service, disruption handling, CS resolution, plus two decline flags) do converge on a single, data-inferable focus: the perceived quality of the airline SERVICE experience across touchpoints and whether it is declining. That gives it more than a grab-bag character. However, coherence is diluted by three columns (food_quality_signal, amenity_and_product_gap, premium_cabin_value_judgment) that belong to a PRODUCT/value dimension rather than service interaction — under a strict single-focus reading these read as aspect enumeration ('here are all the things in the reviews') rather than facets of one focus. Structure is otherwise sound: the service touchpoints form a genuine journey-based decomposition at a useful, non-restating granularity with semantically rich categorical values (not mechanical token/length/bare-sentiment features), but it is weakened by the near-redundant pair service_decline_perception / airline_decline_narrative. Actionability is high: 'which service touchpoint drives dissatisfaction / is service declining' is a concrete, investigable framing an analyst can act on.
